label: Riser Doors
summary: Fire-rated steel access doors to service risers and shafts, supplied and installed.
construction: Steel skins to both faces over an insulated strengthened core, 100 mm thick. Door tray and frame in 1.0 and 1.2 mm Zintec electro-galvanised mild steel. Quick-release heavy-duty pivot hinges welded into the door trays. Multiple-point locking to the active leaf.
_PROVISIONAL: INTERNAL NOTE — never rendered in the interface or the PDF, and not to be pasted into anything client-facing. CONFIRM BEFORE ISSUE. Two different kinds of figure live in this file and they must not be conflated. (1) statedLimits, the option lists, the acoustic figures and the standards come from supplier literature — what a supplier says it makes. (2) testEvidence is what a fire test report actually demonstrates. The tool now derives the size answer from (2) and treats (1) as a fallback that is flagged as unevidenced, which is the whole point: a claimed maximum is not a tested maximum. Still unconfirmed: whether E and EI classifications are offered on riser doors (the literature evidences EW120 for riser doors; E120 and EI60 are quoted for access panels, a different product), and whether periods below 120 are orderable.

statedLimits.source: Supplier literature. Claimed manufacturing envelope, not a tested envelope.

clearOpening.note: Clear opening is the structural opening less 201 mm on width and 75 mm on height.

structuralAllowance.note: Prepare the structural opening 16 mm larger than the ordered door. The frame provides 10 mm of in-frame adjustment, so no packers or mastic are needed.

fireClassificationNote: EW adds control of radiated heat to integrity, reducing the risk of fire spreading by radiation and allowing safer passage past an open riser door on an escape route. Bi-directionally tested to EW120.

options.label: Handing
options.note: Viewed from the access side. For multi-leaf sets this is the active leaf.

options.label: Wall construction
options.note: The fire rating depends on the partition meeting the required fire performance.

choices.label: Euro-cylinder and concealed keyhole
choices.note: Most popular — handles are rarely fitted to flush doors.

choices.label: Concealed keyhole only
choices.note: Square-drive T-key. The keyhole sits behind a spring-loaded flap.

choices.label: Euro-cylinder only
choices.note: Cylinder visible; the last turn of the key operates the latch.

choices.label: Fully concealed
choices.note: Keyhole and euro-cylinder both behind a magnet-held flush flap.

choices.label: Low-resin powder for over-painting
choices.note: Formulated to take emulsion and blend into the surrounding wall. No extra cost.

testEvidence._note: INTERNAL. Read this before changing any number below. The specimen is a single LEAF, not a doorset — the field of direct application in EN 1634-1 Annex B is expressed per leaf, which is why the tool divides the clear opening by the leaf count before testing it against the envelope. The report demonstrates integrity. It does not state an E / EW / EI classification and insulation was not evaluated, so the EW ratings offered elsewhere in this file rest on supplier literature, not on this report. Second gap: supplier literature quotes a corner of 938 x 2750 mm, and 2750 exceeds the 2492 mm that Annex B permits from this specimen, so a second report on a taller specimen must exist. It has been requested and is not held. Until it arrives the tool will correctly report tall leaves as unevidenced.

specimen.reference: Third-party fire test report held on file. Integrity demonstrated; no classification stated; insulation not evaluated.

fieldOfApplication.note: Category B permits the tested leaf to be increased by 15% on width, 15% on height and 20% on area. All three apply at once, so the area cap binds before the linear caps do on anything other than a narrow tall leaf or a wide short one.

leafGeometry.note: Leaf width is taken as the clear opening width divided by the number of leaves, and leaf height as the clear opening height. Meeting stiles overlap by a few millimetres on multi-leaf sets, so this understates leaf width very slightly. Confirm against the manufacturing drawing before order.
